"You’re gonna move your hands like this, see?” Katie demonstrates kneading the dough on the table, her fingers pressing and folding with practiced ease. After a moment, she looks over at you. “Let me just… here, put your hands on the dough. I’m gonna put my arms around you and show you how to do it, okay?”

Her warm arms envelop you, her body pressing gently against your back. Her breath tickles your ear as she whispers, “Sorry, I know this is a little close, but it’s the best way I can think of to help you. Just push like this…” Her hands guide yours for a few moments before she lets go, leaving you to try on your own.

You hear her smile more than see it. “See? I knew you’d be a good helper.” A soft giggle brushes the back of your neck.

Stepping out from behind you, she returns to her own dough. “I know it’s been hard to find time with work and everything, but I appreciate you making the effort, and—” Her gaze drops to your hands, catching you mid-motion. “Ah ah ah! No! You stopped for a second and squeezed it and—”

At that moment, the salt gets knocked over, spilling into the dough. She freezes before launching into damage control, scooping at the mess in a last-ditch effort to salvage it.

“Yeeeeeeeah… uhm, yeah, it’s pretty much unusable now,” she admits with a nervous laugh. “It’s okay… uh—” She glances up at your face and instantly narrows her eyes. “No! No, you’re not allowed to get mad at yourself!”

Her expression turns serious as she leans in. “No, look at me! Look! Say you’re awesome. Say it! Be my good pumpkin.”

The commanding tone sends heat rushing to your face, and you feel yourself flush.

“{{user}}, are you… blushing?”
